concept.literalSynthesis: The Russian-named Jester's Star Musket is loaded with a Terraria Fallen Star and fires a bright star round that arcs downward; when it hits an enemy, a smaller seeking star breaks away.
concept.coreMechanic: Use a ranged musket shot every 32 ticks (about 0.53 seconds). Each active shot requires a Fallen Star and uses Terraria's native ammo selection and consumption rules, including any native ammo-saving hooks. The main projectile deals the musket's authored 31 ranged base damage plus the selected ammo's native contribution, follows a deliberate downward gravity arc, and stops after its first NPC hit. That hit creates one child star whose damage is 35% of the main projectile's live damage; the child turns slowly toward a nearby enemy and expires after one second. This creates a single, bounded follow-up hit per main shot, while making Fallen Stars a recurring combat cost. The musket's source facts show 31 damage, a 32-tick interval, Blue rarity, value 77,600 copper, and generation depth zero; the Fallen Star is a Blue, 2,500-copper consumable material. No progression tier or standalone Fallen Star damage is inferred from those facts.
concept.parentAContribution: The Jester's Star Musket supplies the concrete musket identity, ranged damage class, 31 base damage, 5.25 knockback, 32-tick cadence, and 9-pixel-per-tick projectile-speed reference. Its observed runtime shot was a piercing star arrow; the new downward gravity and Fallen Star ammo requirement are authored mechanics for this synthesis, not claims about that observed shot.
concept.parentBContribution: Terraria's Fallen Star supplies the second identity and is used as the weapon's selected ammo category. Its observed facts include Blue rarity, a 2,500-copper value, and consumable-material status; its damage sentinel does not establish a damage amount. The authored child star is a new effect, not an observed Fallen Star ability.
concept.playerExperience: Aim the musket and fire at the normal cadence. A shot consumes a Fallen Star subject to native ammo-saving rules, arcs downward, and can produce one weaker homing follow-up on its first enemy hit. The arc rewards aiming ahead, while ammunition limits repeat use.

plannedPlayerActions.intent: Fire one cursor-aimed, gravity-arc ranged round using a Fallen Star as ammunition; its first enemy hit creates one slower, weaker homing star. Native ammo selection and consumption govern the recurring cost.

realization.description: Fire with primary use while carrying Fallen Stars. The musket launches a cursor-aimed shot at its base 32-tick interval; each active shot uses Terraria's native Fallen Star ammo selection and conservation rules. The shot follows a downward gravity arc and ends on its first NPC hit. That hit spawns one child star with 35% of the main shot's live damage and knockback; it starts along the shot's travel direction, turns gradually toward a chaseable enemy within 18 blocks, and lasts up to one second. The child can be blocked by tiles and hits each NPC at most once.
realization.playerExperience: The main round is the reliable direct hit; the slower child can add a follow-up when a target remains in range and the path is clear. Fallen Star availability and the native ammo-saving result set the effective firing supply.
realization.selfEvaluation: The primary shot is an active spawn_entity binding and the item explicitly requires fallen_star ammunition. Main and child movement are authored on their respective entities; the main on_hit event spawns one bounded child.
